title: Zeraki Pricing in Kenya: What Schools Actually Pay (2026)
h1: Zeraki Pricing in Kenya: What Schools Actually Pay (2026)
description: Zeraki pricing in Kenya explained — how school software is priced per student, per term or by quote, the hidden costs to watch, and how to compare fairly.
author: SQUL Team
intro: School software pricing in Kenya is deliberately hard to compare: some vendors charge per student, some per school, and others only quote after a demo. This guide explains how **Zeraki pricing** fits the market, what the numbers usually look like as *models* (not vendor figures), and the hidden costs that make a cheap quote expensive. For the shape of the whole market, see [school management system pricing in Kenya](/blog/school-management-system-price-in-kenya).

We will be upfront: we do not publish specific Zeraki figures, because vendors change them and we will not guess. Instead you get the models, the questions, and a fair way to compare any two quotes — including ours.
quickAnswer: Editor's note: competitor pricing changes and is not published consistently. The models described here are generic and illustrative; confirm current Zeraki pricing directly with the vendor. SQUL's own pricing is a free term, then per-term. Last reviewed September 2026.

sections.heading: How school software is priced in Kenya

blocks.text: Almost every Kenyan school-software quote is one of five shapes. Knowing which one you are being offered matters more than the headline number.

rows: A fee for each learner each term
Schools that want cost tied to size
Counts drift; you pay more as you grow
One fee per school per term
Staff time, security and upgrades are on you
Start free, pay per term later
Check the price after the free period

sections.heading: Where Zeraki sits in that market

blocks.text: Zeraki is an established, well-known platform, and like most established vendors it prices through one of the models above — commonly some form of per-student or per-term arrangement, or a tailored quote after a demo. Because it is not published consistently, the honest answer is: **ask them directly, and ask in writing.** Use the questions below so you compare like with like.

blocks.title: Do not trust forum numbers
blocks.text: Prices posted on social media or old blog posts are almost always out of date or for a different scope. Get a written quote with the learner count and modules listed.

sections.heading: The hidden costs nobody puts in the quote

blocks.text: The licence is rarely the whole cost of a school system. Ask about each of these before you sign:

items: **SMS and WhatsApp message costs** — who pays per message, and at what rate?
**M-Pesa / Paybill integration** — is automatic reconciliation included, or a paid add-on?
**Onboarding and training** — is setup free, and how much staff time will it take?
**Data migration** — is importing your existing learner register included?
**Support** — is there a fee for phone support, or a response-time guarantee?
**Per-module upsells** — are timetables, report cards, or analytics in the base plan?

blocks.caption: The true cost is licence plus messages plus setup — the licence alone is misleading.

sections.heading: How to compare two quotes fairly

items.title: Normalise to per-learner, per-term
items.text: Turn every quote into the same unit: total annual cost divided by learners, so a per-school and a per-student quote can be compared.

items.title: Add the message costs
items.text: Estimate your SMS and WhatsApp volume for a term and add it. This is where "cheap" quotes turn expensive.

items.title: Price the features you actually need
items.text: If automatic M-Pesa or report cards are add-ons elsewhere, include them before comparing.

items.title: Ask about the exit
items.text: What happens at year-end? Can you export your data? Is there a lock-in?

blocks.text: SQUL is deliberately simple: **a free term to start, then per-term pricing.** Automatic M-Pesa reconciliation, WhatsApp and SMS messaging, and CBC report cards are core — not paid add-ons — so the quote you see is closer to the cost you pay.

blocks.caption: Messages you would otherwise pay a separate SMS service for are part of the platform.

blocks.text: For a like-for-like feature view, see [SQUL vs Zeraki](/blog/squl-vs-zeraki) and compare the models in [free vs paid school software](/blog/free-vs-paid-school-management-software-kenya).

There is no single “Zeraki price” you can trust from an article — and that is the point. Get written quotes, normalise them to per-learner per-term, add message and integration costs, and price the features you actually need. Do that, and the cheapest option is rarely the one with the lowest headline number.

faqs.question: How much does Zeraki cost in Kenya?
faqs.answer: Zeraki's pricing is not published consistently and changes over time. It is typically some form of per-student or per-term arrangement, or a quote after a demo. Ask the vendor for a written quote covering your learner count and modules.

faqs.question: Is Zeraki priced per student or per school?
faqs.answer: That varies by package and can change, so confirm directly. Many Kenyan school systems use per-student-per-term pricing; some offer a flat or quoted arrangement.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest school management software in Kenya?
faqs.answer: Open-source options are free to license but cost in IT staff and training. SQUL offers a free term then per-term pricing. Compare the total cost, not just the licence.

faqs.question: Are SMS messages included?
faqs.answer: Often not — SMS is frequently a separate cost. Ask who pays per message and at what rate, and add it to your comparison. SQUL includes WhatsApp and SMS messaging in the platform.

faqs.question: Does automatic M-Pesa cost extra?
faqs.answer: At some vendors it is an add-on. At SQUL, automatic M-Pesa reconciliation is core. Always confirm before comparing quotes.

faqs.question: How do I compare two quotes properly?
faqs.answer: Convert both to total annual cost per learner, add SMS/WhatsApp volume, include any add-ons you need, and check exit terms and data export.
